title: What people frame, i
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: The first customer. A fishing license. Wood learns the town by what it puts on the wall.

panels.composition: The frame shop counter. A CUSTOMER, a fisherman, sliding a laminated fishing license across. WOOD.

image.prompt: a weathered fisherman sliding a laminated fishing license across a frame-shop counter to a young man in a chore coat

panels.composition: The license. A number. Fifty years of renewal stickers layered on the back like tree rings.

image.prompt: close-up of an old fishing license with fifty years of renewal stickers layered on its back like tree rings

panels.composition: Wood, choosing a frame with more care than he's shown anything. Cedar. Plain.

characters.pose: holding up a plain cedar frame

balloons.text: Cedar. No mat. It doesn't need help.

image.prompt: a young man holding up a plain cedar frame sample against a fishing license with great care

panels.composition: The fisherman leaving with the framed license under his arm. Wood at the counter, drawing it from memory before it's out the door.

image.prompt: a fisherman walking out of a frame shop with a small framed license under his arm while the young man at the counter sketches it from memory, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The frame-job dailies begin. The town, one wall at a time.
